summary: A pair of steel range towers that have guided ships into Munising Bay since 1908; the rear light was decommissioned in 2019.

notes_for_editor:
Power when new: the NPS brochure says the lanterns were powered by incandescent electric bulbs; LighthouseFriends says the towers first showed fixed red lights from reflector lanterns, with a brick oil house, and says the range was electrified in 1941. The story gives both accounts.
Front tower height: 58 ft (NPS; the Society's record gives 58 ft from base to lantern centre) against 55 ft (LighthouseFriends). The record has 18.0 m. The story gives the NPS figure and notes the difference.
Board's 1905 request: LighthouseFriends says $13,200. A USLHS search snippet (the place page history, not read in full) says $13,500. The story gives no figure; check the USLHS history text before adding one.
Society's record gives the tower material as BRICK & CAST IRON; the NPS and LighthouseFriends both say steel. Not repeated in the story.
Range: the record gives range 12 nm. The NPS brochure says the 1908 lights were visible on the lake for 19 miles (unit not stated; 19 statute miles is about 16.5 nm). Not changed in the record; check the Light List range before changing it.
Status: Rowlett (2019) says the front beacon was replaced by a leading light and the rear light decommissioned. The Visitor's Bureau calls the front tower active; the Society's record says active. The Coast Guard Light List entries (LLNR 7-14575 front, 7-14580 rear) were not read. Current status needs a Light List check before publication.
Light characteristic: the record's F W is not supported by any source read, which all say red. The current characteristic needs the Light List.
Name: the Society spells it Munsing Range. The story uses the NPS and Visitor's Bureau spelling, Munising.
Keepers: only the roster and LighthouseFriends are used. Thomas Hendrickson (1912 to at least 1924) and Floyd Miller's service beyond the roster were not checked further. The archive's roster gives Miller "at least 1960"; LighthouseFriends gives his retirement as 1961.
Grand Island Harbor Lighthouse (1868) is a different station, not in this batch. The story mentions it only as the light the range replaced; the record should not absorb its history.
The Lake Carriers' Association 1908 report is quoted through LighthouseFriends; the original was not read.
The NPS brochure's photo caption about the steamer Herman Hettler (wrecked at Grand Island, 23 November 1926) is not tied to the range in the text, so it is not used.
No storms or wrecks tied to this range were found in the sources read; the storms chapter is omitted.
Photos: none added; not checked for licence.
Not read: the USCG Historian's Munising Range Lights page (the live site is blocked and no archived copy was tried for this station).
Fact-check 2026-10-27: Rowlett's directory (source 4) describes the front light after 2019 as a leading light showing 'continuous light, white, red or green depending on direction'. The story now says so, so the opening no longer says the towers show red lights today. The corrections entry for the characteristic was reworded: F W may be the leading light's setting, so it is not proposed as F R. The NPS brochure's 1908 electric bulbs and LighthouseFriends' 1941 electrification are stated as conflicting; no source read settles the 1908 power source.
